missions.title: A repair or replacement choice
paragraphs: A small appliance stops working. The owner has not compared repair and replacement options. The people involved need enough information to choose a practical response.

One practical option is to request enough information to compare both options. The expected benefit is that the decision can consider cost and expected use. This gives the response a clear purpose that can be checked afterwards.

The people involved can make progress by separating the immediate action from questions that still need an answer. This prevents an incomplete explanation from becoming an unrealistic promise. A brief follow-up can establish whether the proposed response actually helped.

paragraphs: A community wants to avoid wasting water. The suggested message sounds blaming and unclear. The people involved need enough information to choose a practical response.

missions.title: A step-free route
paragraphs: A venue offers a room on an upper floor. The invitation gives no information about lift access. The people involved need enough information to choose a practical response.

Before we go ahead, we agree to confirm the access arrangements before inviting guests. The expected benefit is that guests can decide whether the venue meets their needs. This gives the response a clear purpose that can be checked afterwards.

The response should fit the actual need, rather than simply repeat a familiar routine. Asking one relevant follow-up question can reveal an important detail. The final arrangement should be checked with the people who will need to use it.

paragraphs: A sign-up form asks several questions in one field. Some users are unsure which information is required. The people involved need enough information to choose a practical response.

missions.title: A choice of participation
paragraphs: A workshop asks everyone to answer aloud. Some participants need more time to prepare a response. The people involved need enough information to choose a practical response.
